look for non-segmental, fluffy, or consolidation-like opacities that spare the central perihilar regions.", "Distinguish from pulmonary edema by confirming the pattern is the 'photographic negative' (peripheral/apical) rather than the classic central/bat-wing distribution.", "Differentiate from organizing pneumonia (which is often patchy, migratory, and less strictly peripheral/apical) and sarcoidosis (which typically presents with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and perilymphatic nodules rather than peripheral consolidation)."]}, {"category": "characterization", "trigger": "When evaluating a chest radiograph with an azygos fissure and assessing changes in the expected teardrop-shaped opacity at its caudal end, particularly in the context of pneumothorax, chest tube placement, or mediastinal shift.", "steps": ["Identify the azygos fissure as a curvilinear line in the right upper lung zone.", "Locate the expected position of the azygos vein (teardrop opacity) at the inferior aspect of the fissure.", "Determine if the opacity is absent from its usual location within the fissure.", "Assess for signs of mediastinal shift or lung re-expansion that could displace mediastinal structures.", "Conclude that absence of the opacity within the fissure, in this context, indicates medial displacement of the azygos vein out of the fissure rather than resolution of fluid or collapse of the vein."]}]
